definitionEn: the process of more people moving from the countryside to cities.
existingExample: Rapid urbanisation has put pressure on housing and transport.

definitionEn: a situation in which roads are too full of vehicles.
existingExample: Congestion charges have helped reduce traffic congestion in some city centres.

definitionEn: buses, trains and other services available to everyone.
existingExample: Cheap and reliable public transport encourages people to leave their cars at home.

definitionEn: the basic systems a country needs, such as roads, bridges and power supplies.
existingExample: Many developing countries need to invest heavily in infrastructure.

definitionEn: to travel regularly between home and work.
meaningVi: đi làm hằng ngày; quãng đường đi làm
existingExample: A long daily commute can affect workers' health and productivity.

definitionEn: the uncontrolled spread of a city into the surrounding countryside.
meaningVi: đô thị lan rộng tràn lan
existingExample: Urban sprawl destroys farmland and increases car dependence.

definitionEn: the situation of too many people being in one place.
existingExample: Overcrowding in cities can lead to poor living conditions.

definitionEn: housing that people on average or low incomes can afford.
existingExample: The government has promised to build more affordable housing for young families.

definitionEn: a person walking in a street rather than travelling in a vehicle.
existingExample: Pedestrian zones make city centres safer and more pleasant.

definitionEn: a building with many floors.
existingExample: High-rise apartments allow more people to live on less land.

definitionEn: areas of grass and trees in a town or city.
existingExample: Access to green spaces improves residents' mental health.

definitionEn: the amount of money needed to pay for basic things like food and housing.
existingExample: The rising cost of living is forcing families to move out of the capital.

definitionEn: useful facilities such as shops, parks and hospitals.
existingExample: New housing estates often lack basic amenities such as schools.

definitionEn: where cars are not allowed.
existingExample: Car-free days encourage people to explore their city on foot or by bike.

definitionEn: the movement of people from the countryside to towns and cities.
meaningVi: di cư từ nông thôn ra thành thị
existingExample: Better job opportunities drive rural-urban migration in developing countries.

definitionEn: the process of richer people moving into a poor area and raising prices.
meaningVi: sự cải tạo khu nghèo thành khu đắt đỏ
existingExample: Gentrification often forces long-term residents out of their neighbourhoods.

definitionEn: a part of the road reserved for bicycles.
existingExample: Dedicated cycle lanes make cycling safer and more popular.

definitionEn: the prevention of accidents on roads.
existingExample: Lower speed limits have improved road safety near schools.

definitionEn: having a lot of people living in a small area.
existingExample: Densely populated cities need efficient public transport systems.

definitionEn: harmful or annoying levels of noise.
existingExample: Living near an airport exposes residents to constant noise pollution.

definitionEn: the design and organisation of how towns develop.
existingExample: Poor town planning has led to a lack of parks in many districts.

definitionEn: a place of historical or cultural importance.
existingExample: Mass tourism can damage fragile heritage sites.

definitionEn: a fee that drivers pay to enter a busy city centre.
meaningVi: phí vào khu trung tâm (chống ùn tắc)
existingExample: London introduced a congestion charge to reduce traffic in the city centre.

definitionEn: a vehicle that can drive without a human controlling it.
existingExample: Self-driving cars could reduce accidents caused by human error.

definitionEn: pleasant and suitable for living in.
existingExample: Investment in parks and transport can make cities more liveable.

definitionEn: a very large, important city.
existingExample: Ho Chi Minh City has grown into a bustling metropolis.

definitionEn: a city with more than ten million inhabitants.
existingExample: Rapid rural-to-urban migration is transforming the capital into a sprawling megacity with immense infrastructure demands.

definitionEn: a person who lives in a city.
existingExample: Urban dwellers often have limited access to nature.

definitionEn: a residential area outside a city centre.
existingExample: Families move to the suburbs for more space.

definitionEn: the area around a city where many commuters live.
meaningVi: vành đai dân cư đi làm
existingExample: House prices have risen across the commuter belt.

definitionEn: an overcrowded, poor area of a city.
existingExample: Millions of people live in slums without clean water.

definitionEn: housing built without official permission.
existingExample: Informal settlements often lack basic sanitation.

definitionEn: improving run-down urban areas.
existingExample: Urban regeneration transformed the old docks.

definitionEn: in poor condition through neglect.
existingExample: Investment revived the run-down neighbourhood.

definitionEn: land previously used for industry.
meaningVi: khu đất công nghiệp cũ (để tái sử dụng)
existingExample: Building on brownfield sites protects the countryside.

definitionEn: dividing land into areas for different uses.
existingExample: Strict zoning laws limit the supply of new housing.

definitionEn: with many buildings or people in a small area.
existingExample: High-density housing makes public transport more viable.

definitionEn: not enough homes for the population.
existingExample: Many cities face a serious housing shortage.

definitionEn: the cost of buying homes and land.
existingExample: Soaring property prices exclude young buyers.

definitionEn: someone buying their first home.
existingExample: First-time buyers struggle to save for a deposit.

definitionEn: government limits on how much rent can rise.
existingExample: Rent controls protect tenants but may reduce housing supply.

definitionEn: a person who rents property.
existingExample: Tenants complained about rising rents.

definitionEn: a person who rents out property.
existingExample: Some landlords fail to maintain their properties.

definitionEn: owning the home you live in.
existingExample: Homeownership is falling among young adults.

definitionEn: the outline of buildings against the sky.
existingExample: Skyscrapers dominate the city skyline.

definitionEn: a famous building or place.
existingExample: The bridge is the city's best-known landmark.

definitionEn: areas open to everyone.
existingExample: Squares and parks provide valuable public space.

definitionEn: to close a street to traffic.
existingExample: Municipal authorities plan to pedestrianise the historic district in order to curb air pollution and boost local commerce.

definitionEn: easy and pleasant to walk around.
existingExample: Walkable neighbourhoods encourage healthier lifestyles.

definitionEn: a system that rents bicycles for short trips.
meaningVi: chương trình xe đạp công cộng
existingExample: Bike-sharing schemes reduce short car journeys.

definitionEn: transport systems carrying large numbers of people, such as metros.
meaningVi: vận tải công cộng khối lượng lớn
existingExample: Mass transit systems reduce congestion.

definitionEn: an underground or urban railway.
existingExample: Hanoi opened its first metro line in 2021.

definitionEn: a tram-like urban rail system.
existingExample: Light rail is cheaper to build than an underground system.

definitionEn: a bus system with dedicated lanes.
existingExample: Bus rapid transit offers metro-like speed at a lower cost.

definitionEn: the busiest time for travel.
existingExample: Traffic grinds to a halt during rush hour.

definitionEn: a traffic jam in which nothing can move.
meaningVi: tình trạng kẹt xe toàn bộ
existingExample: An accident caused gridlock across the city.

definitionEn: a narrow point that causes delays.
existingExample: The old bridge is a major traffic bottleneck.

definitionEn: relying heavily on cars.
existingExample: Car-dependent suburbs make life difficult without a car.

definitionEn: having a private car.
existingExample: Rising car ownership increases congestion.

definitionEn: to share a car journey with others.
existingExample: Colleagues carpool to save money and reduce traffic.

definitionEn: booking a car journey through an app.
meaningVi: dịch vụ gọi xe công nghệ
existingExample: Ride-hailing apps are popular in Southeast Asian cities.

definitionEn: an area where polluting vehicles must pay or are banned.
meaningVi: vùng hạn chế xe phát thải cao
existingExample: Low-emission zones improve urban air quality.

definitionEn: using relatively little fuel.
existingExample: Fuel-efficient cars cost less to run.

definitionEn: a vehicle powered by electricity.
existingExample: More charging points are needed for electric vehicles.

definitionEn: a place where electric vehicles are recharged.
existingExample: The city installed hundreds of charging stations.

definitionEn: a charge for using a road or bridge.
existingExample: Drivers pay a toll to use the new expressway.

definitionEn: a wide road for fast traffic.
existingExample: A new expressway links the two cities.

definitionEn: a bridge carrying one road over another.
existingExample: Flyovers were built to ease congestion at major junctions.

definitionEn: a professional who designs how cities develop.
existingExample: Urban planners are designing greener, more compact cities.

definitionEn: a city that uses technology to improve services.
existingExample: Developing a sustainable smart city requires integrating real-time sensor networks with responsive public transport.

definitionEn: systems for clean water and waste removal.
meaningVi: hệ thống vệ sinh môi trường
existingExample: Poor sanitation spreads disease in slums.

definitionEn: collecting, treating and disposing of waste.
existingExample: Rapidly growing cities struggle with waste management.

definitionEn: a person selling goods in the street.
existingExample: Street vendors are part of Hanoi's character.

definitionEn: full of energy and life.
existingExample: Hanoi's Old Quarter is a vibrant area.

definitionEn: full of busy activity.
existingExample: The market is bustling from early morning.

definitionEn: containing people from many countries.
meaningVi: mang tính quốc tế, đa văn hóa
existingExample: London is one of the most cosmopolitan cities in the world.

definitionEn: loneliness experienced by people living in cities.
meaningVi: sự cô đơn ở đô thị
existingExample: Despite the crowds, many city residents suffer from urban isolation.

definitionEn: how good and comfortable someone's life is.
existingExample: Green spaces improve residents' quality of life.

definitionEn: the level of wealth and comfort people have.
existingExample: Cities usually offer a higher standard of living.

definitionEn: too many people living in an area.
existingExample: Overpopulation strains housing and water supplies.

definitionEn: a person who moves to another place to find work.
existingExample: Migrant workers send much of their income home.

definitionEn: pressure caused by excessive demand.
existingExample: Rapid growth puts a strain on public services.

definitionEn: measures that slow traffic, such as speed bumps.
meaningVi: biện pháp giảm tốc giao thông
existingExample: Traffic calming measures make streets safer for children.

definitionEn: the maximum legal speed.
existingExample: Lower speed limits reduce serious accidents.

definitionEn: how easy a place is to reach or use.
existingExample: Stations should improve accessibility for wheelchair users.

definitionEn: a central place where transport routes meet.
existingExample: The central station is a major transport hub.

definitionEn: to move to a new place.
existingExample: Several factories were relocated outside the city.

definitionEn: forcing people to leave their homes.
existingExample: Large infrastructure projects can cause the displacement of residents.

definitionEn: legally forcing someone to leave their home.
meaningVi: sự cưỡng chế ra khỏi nhà
existingExample: Rising rents left many families facing eviction.

definitionEn: a district protected for its historic character.
existingExample: The old town was designated a conservation area.

definitionEn: the historic buildings of a place.
existingExample: Rapid development threatens the city's architectural heritage.

definitionEn: a city area full of buildings with little greenery.
existingExample: Without parks, cities become concrete jungles.

definitionEn: growing food in cities.
existingExample: Urban farming makes use of rooftops and vacant land.

definitionEn: a mass movement of people away from the countryside.
meaningVi: làn sóng rời bỏ nông thôn
existingExample: A rural exodus has left many villages with only elderly residents.

definitionEn: a fall in the number of people in an area.
existingExample: Rural depopulation threatens village schools.

definitionEn: a project funded and run jointly by government and private companies.
existingExample: The new metro line was built through a public-private partnership.

definitionEn: the design and organisation of how cities develop.
existingExample: Poor urban planning has led to a lack of parks in many districts.

definitionEn: A high-capacity urban road designed to carry large volumes of traffic between city centres, suburbs, and highways.
meaningVi: tuyến đường huyết mạch chính của đô thị
existingExample: Dedicated bus lanes along every major arterial road significantly reduced morning travel times for outer-suburb commuters.

definitionEn: The design, manufacture, operation, and commercial management of aircraft and air transport networks.
existingExample: Decarbonising long-haul aviation remains one of the most formidable technical hurdles facing global transport planners.

definitionEn: Crushed stone laid beneath railway sleepers to distribute load and aid drainage, or heavy material used to stabilise ships.
meaningVi: đá dằn đường ray; vật dằn ổn định tàu thủy
existingExample: Extreme summer heatwaves can destabilise railway ballast, compelling operators to impose strict speed restrictions.
